title: The Shrimp That Punches Twice (Mantis Shrimp)
description:
This shrimp punches so fast that the water itself hits its prey a second time 🦐

The peacock mantis shrimp swings its club at up to 23 metres a second, underwater. Muscle alone can't do that, so it latches the arm, loads a saddle-shaped spring and lets go. The water tears into tiny vapour bubbles, and when they collapse they strike the shell again, with sound, heat and faint flashes of light. All in under a thousandth of a second.

Would you keep one in an aquarium? 👇

Source: Patek, Korff & Caldwell, Nature 428, 819-820 (2004).
